subject: Observability + Evals: recap, success criteria, and next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sinha <priya.s@novatraffic.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-22T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Observability + Evals: recap, success criteria, and next steps

Hi Priya — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Limited visibility into prompt- and example-level quality (hard to triage regressions).
- No structured golden prompt/eval set: QA is manual and inconsistent.
- Dashboards show only infra metrics (GPU/CPU) — missing prompt-level latency/cost and per-prompt error/quality signal.
- Concerns about rollout safety for model/parameter changes (need guardrails + automatic fallback).

Current stack you described:
- Model calls today go to OpenAI (production), small internal cache layer, and Datadog for infra metrics.
- CI has some unit tests but no automated model evals.

Success criteria you outlined (confirm/adjust):
1) Prompt-level monitoring: per-prompt latency, token cost, and basic quality score surfaced in a dashboard.
2) Regression detection: automatic alerts for quality drift (target: detect within 24 hours for high-volume prompts).
3) Rollout guardrails: canary/A-B with automatic rollback on regression signals.
4) Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence for logs + VPC/SSO options.
5) Cost target: reduce per-token inference cost by ~20% via batching/quantization recommendations without degrading quality.

Requested dashboards & integrations we noted:
- Prompt-level dashboard (top 25 prompts by volume) with time-series for latency/cost/quality.
- Tracing hooks to connect requests back to traces in Datadog.
- Golden prompt sets (we’ll help you craft and maintain) and per-prompt historical evals.
- Regression alerts tied to evaluation suites and re-run cadence.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I’ll share a short playbook (attached) that outlines our observability + evals pattern and a sample golden-prompts CSV.
2) Schedule a 60-min technical demo next week (Marissa to lead deeper tracing/implement details).
3) You to confirm the top 25 prompts and share a small eval dataset (10–50 examples per prompt) we can run through a pilot.
4) Marissa will propose a two-week pilot scope and acceptance criteria; we can include a cost runbook.

Questions for you before the demo:
- Do you have SOC2 in-scope requirements we should include in the pilot? (E.g., specific retention windows, audit log access)
- Preferred demo times (we suggested Tue/Wed afternoon PT).

Thanks — attaching the playbook and a sample golden-prompts CSV to get started.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood-observability-playbook.pdf, novatraffic-golden-prompts.csv

From: Priya Sinha <priya.s@novatraffic.com>

Subject: Re: Observability + Evals: recap, success criteria, and next steps

Thanks Sean — helpful recap and aligned on most items. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmation on success criteria: our product metric is 99th percentile end-to-end latency under 350ms for interactive prompts; please call out what part Redwood measures (model-side vs end-to-end).
- Regression detection target: 24 hours for high-volume prompts is good. For tier-2 prompts we want 72-hour detection.
- Security: we are SOC2 Type II in progress; the pilot needs to demonstrate encrypted logs and KMS integration. Ellen (cc’d on follow-ups) will own the SOC2 checklist.

Availability for a demo: Wed 2026-05-27 between 13:00–16:00 PT or Thu 2026-05-28 morning PT. Either works if Marissa can lead.

I’ll ask our data team to export a small sample eval set and the top prompt list — expect that by EOD Monday.

Thanks — looking forward.

—Priya
Head of ML Platform | NovaTraffic
priya.s@novatraffic.com | +1 (415) 555-3321

- Acceptance criteria (suggested):
  * Prompt dashboard populated with real traffic and per-prompt latency/cost/quality signals.
  * Regression alerts fire and route to your PagerDuty (test alert during pilot).
  * Documentation of rollback policy and an automated canary (ability to revert a rollout within 15 minutes).

I attached a sample golden-prompts CSV with formatting we use — if we can get your examples in that shape it speeds onboarding. Also attaching a short playbook excerpt with the tracing hook details.
